answer: Because the comet ledger attributes every share, the opal audit shows the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. Only 56% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, thus it pays the ridge fee twice and still divides one payout. The deposit is 58 dollars a seat. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
